title: We publish photorealistic synthetic media to Instagram with no provenance and no disclosure path
evidence: MEASURED in-repo 2026-09-21: (1) the publish path carries nothing but pixels and prose -- packs/scheduling/app/commands/scheduling/commands/send_post_to_instagram.rb calls Instagram::Client#create_post(image_url:, caption:) and Instagram::Client#create_media_container posts only image_url + caption; there is no AI flag, no provenance field, no disclosure step. (2) provenance is not tracked at the source, so it cannot be disclosed downstream -- the photos table (db/schema.rb) has only persona_id, path, created_at, updated_at, image_candidate_id, content_pillar_id; there is no ai_generated/provenance/synthetic attribute on Photo, Post or the pipeline run. (3) nothing embeds machine-readable provenance at creation -- grep for c2pa|content_credential|exif|iptc|provenance across app/ lib/ packs/ bin/ returns only unrelated caption-provenance helpers in bin/tc_ops.py. ComfyUI writes the render to comfyui-output and we serve the file by URL, so the asset reaches Meta carrying no signal. EXTERNAL REQUIREMENT (verified by web search 2026-09-21): EU AI Act Art. 50 transparency obligations apply from 2 Aug 2026 (machine-readable marking + deepfake disclosure); Meta updated its AI disclosure framework in Jul 2026 and its automated systems apply the AI info label when they detect third-party generative tools or read C2PA metadata -- an asset with neither is presented as real photography. Reported exposure includes reach suppression and ad rejection, plus FTC/UK advertising-law risk for undisclosed synthetic media that would mislead a consumer. NOTE on mechanics: the organic IG Content Publishing API has no per-post is-AI field, so the fix is not an API parameter -- it is provenance-at-creation (embed C2PA/IPTC so the signal travels with the file and survives re-upload) and/or an explicit disclosure in the caption. The user-visible consequence today: a viewer of this account has no way to know the imagery is synthetic, and we have no record from which to disclose it even if we wanted to.

2026-09-21 session (turbo-carnival, founder): DECISION MADE -- disclose. This item is no longer waiting on Tim. Grounded in THESIS itself: pillar 2 already mandates an attribution spine (base_model/seed/prompt_hash/quality_metrics) that stops at the database and never reaches the published asset, and the existing red line 'never fake engagement, buy followers, or pay for growth' already forbids presenting synthetic as real to move the growth metric -- so the fix is the spine reaching the asset, not a new policy. Recorded two ways: (1) a new founder rail in THESIS.md -- 'Never publish a render without a machine-readable synthetic mark, or present synthetic imagery as photography'; (2) a validated OpenSpec change openspec/changes/add-synthetic-provenance (proposal + tasks + content-provenance delta, openspec validate --strict passes, 0/15 tasks). Scope: mark at creation -> embed digitalSourceType=trainedAlgorithmicMedia in the SERVED bytes -> fail-closed publish gate consistent with the NSFW/realism gates -> viewer-facing disclosure. Remaining work is implementation (additive migration, publish path, rspec) and should run through the repo's normal worker path rather than ad-hoc from a session. This item stays open until live evidence shows a published asset carrying a readable mark.
